definition: Microbotics (or microrobotics) is the field of miniature robotics, in particular mobile robots with characteristic dimensions less than 1 mm.
details: The term can also be used for robots capable of handling micrometer size components.

explainer.lead: Microbotics is the field of miniature robotics, focused on mobile robots with characteristic dimensions under 1 mm. It matters because robots at that scale can go where conventional machines cannot.

tiers.eli5: These are robots so small that a whole one is tinier than a grain of sand, built to move around and do jobs at that size.
tiers.practitioner: The term also covers robots able to handle micrometer-sized components, so engineers use it for both tiny movers and tiny handlers. The pitfall is scale itself: at under 1 mm, ordinary actuation and control assumptions do not carry over.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as miniature robotics, in particular mobile robots with characteristic dimensions less than 1 mm; the term may also apply to robots capable of handling micrometer-size components.

explainer.example: A mobile robot measuring under 1 mm across counts as a microrobot under the field's size criterion.
